Author - Giovanniland (with Overthinkers)
Forum Thread - https://forum.nationstates.net/viewtopic.php?f=24&t=551112
Proposal Link - https://www.nationstates.net/page=UN_view_proposal/id=giovanniland_1722453928

Cast your vote by reacting to this message. You can also discuss below. Information here may be used to construct an IFV.

:For: = FOR / AYE
:Against: = AGAINST / NAY
:abstain: = TEP ABSTAINS
⏭️ = NO OPINION / PRESENT

I’m for! I know our relationship with TWP has been rocky but the author and nominee, from my memory, are both awesome people who we enjoyed working with before the falling out. Dilber’s accomplishments TWP are comparable to Libertanny’s here IMO and both deserve commendations. I think the point on his WA resolutions is particularly strong.
On one hand, gross TWP
On the other, this is rather commenable
Idk

I think times like these are the perfect opportunity to show we’re the bigger person…er group of people. If we’re willing to forgive and move on, if we’re willing to take the step (as we did in my delegacy) to open the door to talking through our old issues and starting over, and if we’re willing to judge their commendations on their own merits, then they have nothing to hold against us and any step they take in the opposite direction is that much worse. We can show them — we know you voted against Commend Libertanny and all TEP GP commends because of your grudge against us, but we still refuse to do the same. Simply put, we turn the other cheek. It broadcasts to the world our reasonableness and our fairness.

When two regions are opposed and every third party has a choice of sidling closer to one or the other, will they want to move closer to the one throwing fits on the forums and withholding crucial WA votes, or will they prefer the one that is above the pettiness? And then again if we don’t take the first step to bury the hatchet, we may not have any chance at all to succeed in that endeavor. Maybe if we’re this reasonable and fair and we don’t stoop to petty maneuverings, they’ll slowly start to accept us and maybe their opinion of us will turn. But even if it doesn’t we can be content in having the moral high ground.

I may be a naïve idealist but I’m a determined one at that, so I don’t mind putting hope in something so unlikely as things with TWP improving. At best, I’ve seen the dawn before the rest of the world and at worst, nothing changes. Not a bad gamble.

We alone have been trying on that front for years to no response, no matter how much we knock on the door and leave free cookies. I’m down for commending Dilber. It’s folly to continue to want to appease a TWP that long decided it was no longer listening.
I guess, but we can still have the moral high ground by continuing to show grace.
Even if TWP doesn't want to like us, we don't have to waste energy *dis*liking *them*, yk
writing ifv now

*Dilber, quite plainly and simply, is a highly commendable nominee. Their work in TWP is admirable and comparable to that of some of the commended greats of TEP and other feeders. In various instances, particularly as Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Delegate, Dilber has served the West Pacific and its people with strong foreign policy decisions, which are captured by author Giovanniland and co-author Overthinkers quite well in various clauses of the commendation. Their domestic accomplishments, such as engineering a TWP Delegate's lead in world endorsements, are equally noteworthy. Even so, the strongest part of the commendation describes Dilber's success in the august World Assembly, through tireless authorship and recognition that should not go unnoticed. The East Pacific acknowledges its past foreign affairs disagreements with the West Pacific, but cannot deny Dilber's accomplishments and the worthiness of this commendation. As such, we vote FOR.*
@Aurora, Desuwa of Umapyoi ^
